verdict.summary: There is no self-serve console for Mercury API OAuth clients. You can't connect even your own account until Mercury approves you as a partner through a private review that weighs security, use-case fit and regulatory factors. After approval, Mercury issues the client ID and secret by hand, encrypted to your GPG key. The one shortcut is Mercury's hosted MCP server, which supports Dynamic Client Registration and needs no pre-approval.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 2-4 hours (form, legal URLs, GPG key, Composio config, testing)
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Only after Mercury approves you (no published timeline). Through the MCP server with Dynamic Client Registration: minutes.
verdict.approval_wait: Not published. Mercury says timelines vary with integration complexity and it may ask for more information.

steps.title: Choose API OAuth or the MCP server
steps.detail: Mercury API OAuth (oauth2.mercury.com) needs partner approval before any connection works. Mercury's hosted MCP server (mcp.mercury.com) supports Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591): your client gets its own client_id at runtime with no pre-approval. If you need a Composio-brokered API connection, continue with the steps below.
gotchas: For MCP registration, client_name must not begin with the word 'Mercury' or registration fails.
For MCP, a web app should use an https redirect URI and omit token_endpoint_auth_method so Mercury returns a client secret.

steps.title: Draft the partner application content
steps.detail: Draft the answers Mercury's form asks for: company name and website, company address, a company description, details of the product being integrated, and your intended API use. Be specific about what data you read and why, because Mercury weighs security, use-case fit and regulatory considerations.

steps.title: Submit Mercury's OAuth partner form
steps.detail: Open the form linked from Mercury's 'Integrations with OAuth2' page and submit your application. There is no self-serve developer console for Mercury OAuth.

steps.title: Wait for Mercury's review
steps.detail: Mercury reviews the request. Timelines vary with integration complexity, and Mercury may ask for more information.

steps.title: Prepare legal URLs, logo and a GPG key
steps.detail: Publish links to your terms of service, privacy policy and logo. Generate a GPG key pair and export the public key so Mercury can deliver credentials securely. Keep the private key safe yourself.

steps.title: Send redirect URIs and app details to Mercury
steps.detail: After approval, send Mercury your production redirect URI, any dev/test redirect URIs, your terms/privacy/logo links and your GPG public key. Use Composio's callback URL as the production redirect URI.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Mercury registers redirect URIs on its side, so changing them later means contacting Mercury again.

steps.title: Receive and decrypt the client credentials
steps.detail: Mercury sends the client ID and client secret through a secure channel, along with credentials for a sandbox test client. Decrypt them with your GPG private key and store them in a secrets manager.

steps.title: Configure a custom OAuth connection in Composio
steps.detail: There is no Mercury toolkit in Composio, so set up a custom OAuth auth config using Mercury's client ID and secret and the authorize endpoint https://oauth2.mercury.com/oauth2/auth. Request the scopes 'read offline_access' (space-separated). Use PKCE with code_challenge_method S256 if your setup supports it.
gotchas: The token endpoint URL wasn't confirmed in the research. Copy it from Mercury's 'obtain the tokens' reference.
Without offline_access you get no refresh token, and access tokens expire after 1 hour.

steps.title: Test the flow against the sandbox
steps.detail: Run a test authorization with the sandbox test client and call api-sandbox.mercury.com. Check that you get an access token and a refresh token, and that refreshing works.
gotchas: Sandbox tokens are rejected by production api.mercury.com, so switch both the client and the API host together.

steps.title: Connect production accounts
steps.detail: Switch to the production client and connect your own Mercury account, then customer accounts. If you need write access, plan for the IP allowlist that Mercury requires on Read and Write tokens.
gotchas: Tokens unused for 45 days are reportedly deleted, and unused write permissions are downgraded.

scopes.effect: Read access to account and transaction data. This is enough for read-only dashboards.
Returns a refresh token, which you need for continued access after the 1-hour access token expires.

blockers.symptom: "The requested OAuth 2.0 Client does not exist." at oauth2.mercury.com
blockers.cause: Mercury hasn't provisioned your client ID. API OAuth clients exist only after partner approval.
blockers.fix: Submit the partner form and wait for Mercury to send credentials, or use the MCP server with Dynamic Client Registration.

blockers.cause: The MCP client_id isn't registered, or registration failed (for example, client_name starts with 'Mercury').
blockers.fix: Register through Dynamic Client Registration first, with a client_name that doesn't start with 'Mercury'.

blockers.symptom: Production API rejects a token that worked in testing
blockers.cause: The token came from the sandbox (api-sandbox.mercury.com) environment.
blockers.fix: Use the production client credentials and the production API host.

blockers.symptom: Write calls fail or money-movement operations aren't available
blockers.cause: Only read and offline_access are documented as API OAuth scopes (per third-party analysis). Write tokens also need an IP allowlist.
blockers.fix: Design for read-only access through OAuth, or use the MCP write scopes, which still need in-app approval in Mercury.

composio.note: Composio has no Mercury toolkit and no managed OAuth app, so you can't start on managed auth. Every Composio-brokered Mercury API connection needs your own Mercury-approved client ID and secret, with Composio's callback URL registered by Mercury as a redirect URI. Check Composio's custom-OAuth support for Mercury yourself before you commit.
